text:
Jamie Benn reached 1,000 career points this month, a milestone that belongs on the short list of great Stars careers, and the night was a reminder of how long he has carried this franchise. Right now, though, the one carrying Dallas is in net.

Jake Oettinger has a league-best five shutouts, the latest a 33-save 1-0 win over Pittsburgh. Over his last five starts he is at .949, saving 8.9 goals above expected. As a team, the Stars have allowed almost 14 fewer goals than their chances deserved, and that is why they are 15-7-2 with 32 points and 7-2-1 in their last 10.

Strip the goaltending out and this is an ordinary team. Dallas gets 50% of the expected goals at 5v5 and has scored about 8.6 fewer goals than its chances deserved. Our expected points say 26.2, a luck gap of 5.8. The finishing should come back with Mikko Rantanen, Wyatt Johnston and Jason Robertson in the lineup; the saves may not stay this good.

Robertson is playing through another contract year, and a reported $125 million offer from Seattle has kept his name in the headlines. He offered no comment on it and, per the headlines, is happy with the Stars "right now." Miro Heiskanen scored an overtime winner against Vegas in his return.

Our simulations still give Dallas an 80% playoff chance. What to watch: whether the shooters warm up before Oettinger cools off.
headline: Oettinger is holding up the standings
